source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables

summary: sR is a statistical corrector component that captures correlations between register values and branch directions. It generates a 12-bit digest from the values of recently written logical registers using a Tomasulo-like tracking table. For each of 8 register banks, it evaluates available registers and selects the single most useful one using a usefulness weight table (UT). The selected digest is then hashed with the PC to index prediction weight tables (WT), contributing a scaled sum to the final statistical corrector output.

state.name: sR_WT
state.organization: 8 banks, 3 tables per bank (WT0, WT1, WT2)
state.indexing: PC + register digest hashed to h0, h1, h2

state.name: sR_UT
state.organization: 8 banks, 3 tables per bank (UT0, UT1, UT2)
state.entry_format: Vector of signed weights (wt_bits), one per logical register

state.name: sR_RegTable
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (max(rob_idx_bits, 12) bits), decay_ctr (decay_ctr_bits bits)

state.name: sR_InFlightState
state.organization: FIFO queue, one entry per in-flight branch
state.entry_format: Bitmask of valid registers at prediction time

algorithms.name: allocate_register
algorithms.notes: Decay counter is decremented globally on every decode to eventually invalidate stale digests.

algorithms.name: write_register_digest
algorithms.notes: Calculates the digest based on the register type and writes it to the payload. Only updates if the ROB index matches.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.pseudocode:
for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
  sR_InFlightState[branch.rob_index][r] = sR_RegTable[r].valid

sR = 0
for b in 0 .. num_banks - 1:
  u_idx0 = hash_ut(PC, 0) % ut0_entries
  u_idx1 = hash_ut(PC, 1) % ut1_entries
  u_idx2 = hash_ut(PC, 2) % ut2_entries
  
  max_u = -99999
  best_reg = -1
  
  for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
    if (r % num_banks) == b and sR_RegTable[r].valid == 1:
      u_sum = sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][r] + sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][r] + sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][r]
      if u_sum > max_u:
        max_u = u_sum
        best_reg = r
        
  bank_sum = 0
  if best_reg != -1:
    digest = sR_RegTable[best_reg].payload
    w_idx0 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 0) % wt0_entries
    w_idx1 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 1) % wt1_entries
    w_idx2 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 2) % wt2_entries
    bank_sum = sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] + sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] + sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2]
  
  if max_u > 0:
    sR = sR + int(bank_sum * useful_multiplier)
    
return sR
algorithms.notes: Selects the most useful valid register per bank to look up the weight tables.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.pseudocode:
for b in 0 .. num_banks - 1:
  num_available = 0
  for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
    if (r % num_banks) == b and sR_InFlightState[branch.rob_index][r] == 1:
      num_available = num_available + 1
      
  if num_available > 0:
    chosen_idx = random_int() % num_available
    current_idx = 0
    chosen_reg = 0
    for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
      if (r % num_banks) == b and sR_InFlightState[branch.rob_index][r] == 1:
        if current_idx == chosen_idx:
          chosen_reg = r
        current_idx = current_idx + 1
        
    u_idx0 = hash_ut(PC, 0) % ut0_entries
    u_idx1 = hash_ut(PC, 1) % ut1_entries
    u_idx2 = hash_ut(PC, 2) % ut2_entries
    
    u_delta = calculate_utility_delta(branch)
    sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    
    digest = sR_RegTable[chosen_reg].payload
    w_idx0 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 0) % wt0_entries
    w_idx1 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 1) % wt1_entries
    w_idx2 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 2) % wt2_entries
    
    w_delta = 1 if branch.direction == 1 else -1
    sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] = saturate(sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] + w_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] = saturate(sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] + w_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2] = saturate(sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2] + w_delta, wt_bits)
algorithms.notes: Randomly selects one register from those available at prediction time to update its usefulness and weight.

algorithms.name: recovery
algorithms.notes: Without a full Tomasulo RAT snapshot, recovery conservatively clears pending writes matching squashed ROBs. Completed wrong-path digests (valid=1) are left to decay naturally.

algorithms.name: extract_fp_sign_and_exp
algorithms.notes: Extracts the sign bit and high-order exponent bits based on the classified FP format.

host_interfaces.description: The exact 64-bit value produced by the instruction to compute the digest.
host_interfaces.fallback: Supply zero as the digest or do not update the register table for this instruction.

host_interfaces.need: instruction destination logical register ID and ROB index at decode
host_interfaces.description: To track which in-flight instruction will write each logical register.
host_interfaces.fallback: Omit tracking for instructions missing this information.

host_interfaces.description: To determine the correct digest generation method.

host_interfaces.need: notification of pipeline squash with squashed ROB indices
host_interfaces.description: To invalidate pending register writes from squashed instructions.
host_interfaces.fallback: Allow pending writes to complete and briefly pollute the digest table until they decay.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: sR_WT: 43008 bits, sR_UT: 9360 bits, sR_RegTable: 1495 bits, sR_InFlightState: 16640 bits
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Table 3 of the paper claims 53863 bits for sR. My total is 70503 bits. I am over by 16640 bits. The paper's total exactly covers WT, UT, and RegTable (43008 + 9360 + 1495 = 53863). It omits the 16640 bits needed for sR_InFlightState to snapshot the 65 valid bits per in-flight branch, which the update algorithm requires to know which registers were available at prediction time. Naming the host as the provider does not remove this from the budget at iso-storage. The 'val' variable is provided by the host exactly at instruction completion when the digest is generated, so it is not carried from prediction and consumes no storage budget.

unit_tests.name: decay_counter_walks_down
unit_tests.given: An instruction completes and writes a register via write_register_digest, setting sR_RegTable decay_ctr to its maximum value of (1 << decay_ctr_bits) - 1. Then (1 << decay_ctr_bits) subsequent instructions are decoded via allocate_register.
unit_tests.expect: decay_ctr reaches 0 after (1 << decay_ctr_bits) - 1 decodes, and on the next decode the register's valid bit in sR_RegTable is cleared to 0.

unit_tests.name: int_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: An INT instruction completes with value 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 via write_register_digest.
unit_tests.expect: sR_RegTable payload receives the XOR-folded digest computed using count_leading_zeros (0) and count_trailing_zeros (4), with valid set to 1.

unit_tests.name: predict_selects_most_useful
unit_tests.given: sR_RegTable has valid digests for registers 0 and 8 (both in bank 0). sR_UT has a higher summed usefulness weight for register 8 than register 0.
unit_tests.expect: predict evaluates bank 0 using the digest of register 8 to index sR_WT, ignoring register 0.

unit_tests.name: update_random_selection
unit_tests.given: A branch commits via update, and its sR_InFlightState shows multiple registers were valid in bank 0 at prediction time.
unit_tests.expect: Only one randomly chosen register from bank 0 has its corresponding sR_UT and sR_WT entries modified.

unit_tests.name: recovery_clears_pending
unit_tests.given: An instruction allocates register 5, leaving it valid=0 and payload=ROB_ID. Then a pipeline squash occurs via recovery with that ROB_ID.
unit_tests.expect: sR_RegTable register 5 retains valid=0 but has its payload cleared to 0.

open_questions: [/algorithms/1/pseudocode] U4: FP register format classification and placement is ambiguous. Assumed bits are right-aligned at digest bit 3 as drawn.

The paper does not state the exact Tomasulo RAT recovery mechanism for sR_RegTable on a pipeline squash. Assumed a lightweight policy that leaves valid wrong-path digests to naturally decay, while clearing pending (valid=0) entries matching squashed ROBs.

[/algorithms/3/pseudocode] The exact utility delta calculation for sR_UT during update is unstated. Assumed a standard usefulness update based on whether the bank's prediction alone matched the overall branch outcome.

[/unit_tests/0] The register's digest is invalidated after 255 subsequent instructions are decoded. The paper says: "RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded" The correction did not land, so this field still says what it said -- resolve it before implementing.
[/state/3] How many in-flight branches should the predictor track state for, given it is not explicitly budgeted in the storage tables?
[/parameters/11] What is the maximum number of in-flight branches the predictor tracks, given the paper only states overall ROB sizes?
[/algorithms/3/trigger] At what pipeline stage is the register predictor trained? Also raised at /parameters/15.
[/state/1/indexing] sR_UT is indexed by the skewed PC. (reviewer cited unverifiable evidence; treat as assumed)
[/state/3] What hardware structure is used to buffer the 'available at prediction time' valid bits until the branch trains?
[/unit_tests/4] How does the register tracker handle pipeline flushes? Does it clear pending ROB indices in the payload?

[/unit_tests/4] How should the Tomasulo-like tracking table be recovered on a pipeline squash? The paper states this is future work, leaving the required squash information from the host undefined. Also raised at /algorithms/4/pseudocode, /host_interfaces/3.

[/algorithms/2/pseudocode] [source I10: Figure 5 (c) Proposed Register Components] the input marks this INFERRED -- a reading of the figure's layout that the paper never states -- so whatever the spec derives from it is an assumption and not a fact: bank membership. Bank 0's register list "R0, R8, R16, ... R64" is a stride-8 sequence, i.e. bank i holds the logical registers r with r mod 8 == i. Bank 0 therefore holds 9 registers (R0..R64) and banks 1..7 hold 8 each, totalling 65 - matching the "eight or nine logical registers" of Section 4.2, the "9x6bit" UT entry annotation, and the factor 65 in Table 3. Also raised at /parameters/14.

[/algorithms/2/pseudocode] [source I11: Figure 5 (c) Proposed Register Components] the input marks this INFERRED -- a reading of the figure's layout that the paper never states -- so whatever the spec derives from it is an assumption and not a fact: the multiplier is PER BANK, not global. The "x0 or x2.5" stage is drawn inside the bank 0 box, downstream of that bank's WT Sigma and upstream of the cross-bank Sigma. Structurally it occupies the same position as "x1 or x2" in panel (a) and "x1 or xM" in panel (b), both of which are explicitly driven by a "Useful" signal from the UT. Reading: each bank's contribution is scaled by 2.5 when that bank's usefulness is positive and suppressed entirely (x0) when it is not; the eight scaled per-bank contributions are then summed to give sR.

[/algorithms/1/pseudocode] [source I15: Figure 6 (b) FP registers] the input marks this INFERRED -- a reading of the figure's layout that the paper never states -- so whatever the spec derives from it is an assumption and not a fact: semantics agree with the prose: in each IEEE-754 format the named slice is exactly the sign bit followed by the high-order exponent bits (8 of 11 for FP64, 5 of 8 for FP32, 2 of 5 for FP16). Also raised at /algorithms/5/pseudocode.

[/state/2] The sR_InFlightState structure requires 16,640 bits of dedicated storage. The paper says: "sR: Register | 6 x (2^7 + 2^8 + 2^9) x 8 | 6 x 65 x (2^3 + 2^3 + 2^3) | { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65 | 53863" The correction did not land, so this field still says what it said -- resolve it before implementing. Also raised at /state/3.
[/unit_tests/4] What is the exact behavior of sR_RegTable on a pipeline squash? Is the payload cleared to 0, or is the state restored from a snapshot?

[/algorithms/1/pseudocode] [source U3: Figure 6 (a) INT registers] the input marks this UNCERTAIN, so it must not be resolved by assumption: count encoding. Each count field is 6 bits, but a 64-bit register can have 0..64 leading (or trailing) identical bits, which needs 7 bits. The figure does not say whether the count saturates at 63, is taken modulo 64, or counts bits matching the sign bit (which caps at 63 naturally). The prose "the count of leading zeros (or ones)" also does not say how the zero/one case is distinguished - whether one extra bit encodes which, or whether the count is simply of bits equal to the MSB (resp. LSB). Also raised at /unit_tests/1, /parameters/13.
